carry_definition.formula: C(x) is the longest run of consecutive LSD-first positions affected by nonzero carry while adding the canonical words for x and W(x).

canonicalization.digit_index: LSD-first: index i is the coefficient of 3^i, matching add_with_trace
canonicalization.leading_zeros: encode and from_digits_lsd strip canonical leading zeros
canonicalization.negatives: encode is sign-aware; C is computed on encode(x) and encode(W(x))
canonicalization.digit_cancellation: A position is affected iff carry_in != 0 or carry_out != 0. Opposite-trit cancellation with carry_in = carry_out = 0 is not a carry event. A nonzero final_carry creates an extra MSD position that counts.
canonicalization.zero: encode(0) is the one-digit itinerary (0); C(0)=0
canonicalization.deterministic: the same integer always yields the same C

candidate_statements.name: carry_bounds_length_growth
candidate_statements.exact_statement: C(x) >= max(0, bt_length(T(x)) - bt_length(x)) for the one-step addition T(x)=x+W(x)
candidate_statements.motivation: A canonical word sum grows in length only when carry reaches a new MSD. Carry-chain length is therefore a lower bound on length growth.
candidate_statements.relevant_domain: integers with a defined one-step reverse-plus-add successor
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact carry-to-length obstruction from the addition mechanism
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed whose canonical length grows by more than C(x)

candidate_statements.name: zero_carry_preserves_length
candidate_statements.exact_statement: C(x)=0 implies bt_length(T(x))=bt_length(x) for the one-step addition T(x)=x+W(x)
candidate_statements.motivation: If no position is affected by carry, the digitwise sum never rewrites. The only remaining length change would be leading-digit cancellation, so zero carry should preserve canonical length exactly.
candidate_statements.relevant_domain: integers with C(x)=0 and a defined one-step successor
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact zero-carry simplification of the reverse-plus-add word
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed with C(x)=0 whose canonical length changes
candidate_statements.failure_mechanism: Zero carry still changes canonical length: C(2)=0, W(2)=-2, 2->0, bt_length 2->1. Opposite-trit cancellation from reverse-as-negation collapses the itinerary without carry.

candidate_statements.name: positive_carry_forces_length_plus_one
candidate_statements.exact_statement: C(x)>0 implies bt_length(T(x))-bt_length(x)=1 for the one-step addition T(x)=x+W(x)
candidate_statements.motivation: If carry were the hidden coordinate of representation change, a nonzero chain would force the only nontrivial one-step length delta available to an itinerary sum: growth by exactly one trit.
candidate_statements.relevant_domain: integers with C(x)>0 and a defined one-step successor
candidate_statements.expected_yield: a one-dimensional carry law determining successor length
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed with C(x)>0 whose length delta is not +1
candidate_statements.failure_mechanism: Positive carry does not force +1 length: C(5)=2, 5->-6 has bt_length 3->3 (delta 0).
